messages:
Sara Nguyen: paging — spike of 5xxs on /v1/generate in us-east, alerting customers. dashboard shows error rate ~28% last 6m. tagging oncall.

oncall-bot: Pager duty triggered -> Mike Patel (oncall) assigned. Incident channel created. Severity: P1.

Mike Patel: looking. can someone share recent deploys? any config pushes to routing/config service?

Sara Nguyen: no deploys in last hour from ci. we did push a routing flag at 02:12 UTC yesterday that rolled through canary but should be stable.

Tim O'Leary: seeing 500s with trace id pattern trace=gen-*. logs show "kvcache miss -> fallback" then downstream 502s. suspects data plane latency. but console shows control plane accepted new routing TTL=10s at 02:12.

Anya Kuznetsova: customer outbound tickets: 2 customers reported timeouts, one internal e2e flagged degraded latency. sending customer impact note after triage.

Leo Chen: grabbing pod logs from us-east runtime nodes. command I ran: `kubectl -n prod logs -l app=runtime -c inference --since=10m | grep -i error | tail -n 200`

Leo Chen: log snippet: 
```
2026-03-15T14:24:31Z runtime[pod-42] ERROR kvcache: propagate_failed key=cfg:route:us-east reason=stale_version
2026-03-15T14:24:32Z runtime[pod-42] WARN fetcher: retrying config pull (attempt=3) http 504
2026-03-15T14:24:33Z runtime[pod-42] ERROR serve: generation aborted: upstream 502
```

Mike Patel: interesting — control plane says config applied but runtime is logging propagate_failed and 504s pulling config. sounds like propagation problem (control plane -> dataplane).

Tim O'Leary: can we confirm console state vs actual config on pods? run `curl http://localhost:15000/flags` on a runtime and `curl https://controlplane.internal/api/configs/route/us-east` from control plane to diff versions.

Leo Chen: ran both: control plane returns `version: v42, ttl:10s`; runtime flags show `applied_version: v41, ttl:30s`. so runtime still on older config.

Anya Kuznetsova: hypothesis: config propagation stalled due to intermittent control plane cache errors -> data plane falling back to older TTL leading to routes that cause high fanout and 5xxs.

Mike Patel: mitigation idea: trigger a coordinated push to force propagation + restart watcher on runtime nodes. quick mitigation: roll a config bump (no behavior change) to v43 to force sync, and restart fetcher threads on affected pods.

Sara Nguyen: agree. who will apply the bump? I can submit a no-op config change. will notify customers.

Tim O'Leary: i'm going to exec into the worst pod and restart the config-watcher process to clear the transient failure. `kubectl -n prod exec -it pod-42 -- pkill -HUP config-watcher`

Leo Chen: I will roll the no-op bump to v43 now. patch: `PATCH /api/configs/route/us-east {"meta":"noop-bump-2045123456"}`

deploy-bot: deploy request accepted -> config route/us-east -> target version v43 -> rollout starting.

Mike Patel: deploying now. after v43 hits, watch error-rate and kvcache logs. set a check in 2m.

(2m pass)

Leo Chen: control plane shows v43 active. runtime pods are gradually reporting `applied_version: v43` now. first pod changed at logs: `2026-03-15T14:26:01Z applied config v43`.

Tim O'Leary: error-rate trending down. customers still with a few 500s but overall from 28% -> 6% in last 5m. good.

Anya Kuznetsova: I'll draft customer comms: small percentage still affected but mitigation in progress. pinging support to attach logs.

Mike Patel: next: preserve timelines and artifacts for RCA. Leo/Tim — can you both export logs (runtime + controlplane) from 14:10-14:30 UTC to /tmp/incident-2045123456 and snapshot config versions?

Leo Chen: done. artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-incident/2045123456/{runtime-logs,cp-logs,config-diff}.tar.gz

Tim O'Leary: preliminary RCA notes in thread: sequence = control plane accepted config v42 -> some control plane cache nodes returned 504s on propagation -> runtime fetcher logged propagate_failed and fell back to v41 -> runtime behavior with older TTL increased request amplification on a subset of routes -> downstream 502s/5xx. root cause candidates: 1) transient cache layer overload in control plane, 2) a fetcher retry bug that didn't backoff correctly, 3) race between canary rollout and cache eviction.

Mike Patel: tagging severity:P1 -> keep incident open until stable for 30m. action items: (A) reliability: add stronger retry/backoff and better instrumentation on fetcher (owner: Tim), (B) ops: add alert when propagate_failed spikes (owner: Leo), (C) platform: add metric comparing control-plane advertised version vs dataplane applied_version (owner: Sara).

Anya Kuznetsova: assigning customer follow-up to support; i will send a status update in 15m.

deploy-bot: rollout complete -> 100% v43.

Mike Patel: handing off to Tim for RCA write-up and timeline compaction. I'm going to grab a break but will remain reachable. Please update thread with timeline entries and hypothesis resolution. :thumbsup:

Tim O'Leary: taking over. I'll compile timeline and submit a postmortem draft in `/docs/incidents/2045123456-postmortem.md`. Also will include the config diff and logs. closing note: evidence points to propagation/cache transient failure as primary vector; further investigation on fetcher retry logic required.

Sara Nguyen: thanks team. preserving logs and marks. closing to be decided after RCA draft. :white_check_mark:
